items.note: A yolk header band with a gentle sag arc, a bold tight heading and a compact disc, cloud and sparkle cluster sits above filter pills with category dots (active ink pill with white dot) and cream borderless cards. Each card has a distinct crescent-shaded pictogram cover (tote, backpack, duffel, sweater, mug, skillet). Next to the reference's warm cream panels and confident type it reads as the same family; the header cluster is small and formulaic compared with the reference's composed vignettes, but it now overlaps tightly instead of scattering.

The band keeps its hue and arc, but the art cluster drops to its own row under the left-aligned text, so the band fills about 600px of mostly empty yellow. The nav wraps to a second row under the logo and cart pill. The reference's phone has one compact header row and centered hero text, so this first screen is noticeably looser and cruder, though the pills and filters below are faithful.

Night version: navy page, indigo cards, indigo cream-equivalent pills, a white active pill and a white cart pill, matching the reference's night palette logic (white pill on navy). The yolk band and saturated covers stay full strength. Close in craft to the light page, with the same small stamped band cluster.

Same structure as the light phone screen on navy and indigo. The night tones are right, but the same tall band with the cluster stacked below the text and the two-row header make the first screen sparse and less considered than the reference's compact, centered phone hero.

A yolk header band with breadcrumb, h2 title and a hexagon-plus-pill cluster sits directly above a half-width yolk cover holding a well-drawn crescent-shaded tote. Two large same-hue fields fill the first screen, which the reference never does: it pairs one field with warm white or cream. Option tiles are outlined boxes with arbitrary glyphs (a target, dots), where the reference picks each row glyph for its label. The blue add-to-cart pill on its ledge and the ink price hierarchy are right.

The cover now follows the title on phones (the rc.1 gap is closed), but a tall yolk band, with the cluster on its own row and lots of empty field, runs straight into a full-width yolk cover. The whole first screen is one yellow block with no white between, unlike the reference's single field per screen.

Navy page with indigo option tiles and stepper circles that correctly follow the night palette. The yolk band and yolk cover still stack as two big saturated fields in one viewport, so the page reads loud and flat instead of the reference's calm navy with one accent field.

As on the light phone: the item cover is correctly placed after the title, but the yolk band and the yolk cover fill the whole first screen, broken only by a navy gap. The hierarchy between page header and product image is lost.

A yolk band then a large green cover with a nicely crescent-shaded sweater: two large saturated fields in one viewport, against the reference's one-field rule. Size tiles are outlined boxes with unrelated glyphs (target, two dots, three dots, zigzag). The type scale, pills and ledges are faithful.

Title, then the green cover directly after (good), but the over-tall yolk band, with its cluster on a separate row, plus a full-width green field means two saturated blocks fill the phone screen. The reference keeps one field and lets cream or white breathe.
The night palette is applied cleanly to the tiles, stepper and text. Still a yolk band directly over a large green cover in the same viewport, and size glyphs that don't relate to their labels.
The same stacking as the light phone page on navy: a tall yolk band with stacked art, then a green cover. Recognisably the system, but cruder in hierarchy than the reference's phone screens.

A blue header band (cart area hue, with a disc, cloud and sparkle) above a cream empty-state panel. The panel holds only a lone two-dot glyph, a title, one line and an ink pill, beside a blue panel of pale-tint chips listing invented cart lines and a total. The reference's empty and feature panels carry a real composition; here a second blue field sits right under the blue band, and the fake order lines contradict the empty message.

A tall blue band with its cluster stacked under the text, then a cream panel with a two-dot glyph and an ink pill. Below that, a blue panel of tinted chips with invented item names and prices. It is recognisable, but the empty state is thin and the fake preview reads as cart contents.

A navy page with an indigo empty panel and a white pill (right for night). The same lone dot pair and the same blue preview panel of invented line items and a total sit beside the blue band, so two blue fields and fake data compete with the actual empty message.

The night tones are correct, but the empty state is the thin dot-pair glyph plus a blue panel listing made-up cart lines. It is weaker than the reference's composed panels and misleading on an empty cart.

findings.summary: Every empty cart renders a 'preview of the filled screen' as invented line items with names, options, prices and a total in tinted chips on a saturated panel, right beside the 'your cart is empty' message. The decoration reads as real cart data, and the panel adds a second blue field under the blue band. The empty state's own art is a lone two-dot glyph, where the reference carries a composed piece.
findings.promptFix: Remove the empty-state preview from the vignette's places. An empty state never shows sample records, names, prices or totals, real-looking or faded: it shows one shape-kit composition of the area's subject (or a size.glyphLg glyph), the title, one line and one ink pill, on a panel in the area hue, or cream when a saturated field is already in view. A two-dot or single-disc mark is never the whole empty-state art.
findings.specRule: Where. Hero and feature sections of front pages, onboarding and feature tours; an empty state as a 40%-opacity preview of the filled screen; a bubble holding the pop-dots glyph while an answer loads.

findings.summary: On product detail pages the area-hue header band sits directly above a large item cover in a saturated category hue (often the same hue), so two large saturated fields fill the first screen on desktop and the whole phone screen. The reference holds one field per view and lets warm white or cream separate it from the next colored element, which keeps the title and the product image distinct.
findings.promptFix: A detail page whose item has a large cover (wider than a third of the content) uses a cream header band (indigo at night) with the area hue only on its nav dot, tag and cluster, so the cover is the screen's one saturated field. Never stack a saturated header band and a saturated cover or panel in the same viewport, and never let two adjacent fields share a hue.

findings.summary: On phones the header band's shape cluster drops onto its own row under left-aligned text, so the band grows to roughly a third of the screen of mostly empty field, and the nav wraps to a second row under the logo and cart pill. The reference's phone keeps one compact header row and a centered hero whose art tucks into the band's corner.
